source: Patients were followed for the primary end point of appropriate ICD firing due to VA.
evidence: This is a statement about the study's primary outcome measure.

claim: Of the 26 HCM patients, 13 (50%) had known VA episodes based on appropriate ICD firing.
source: As stated above, of the 26 HCM patients, 13 (50%) had known VA episodes based on appropriate ICD firing.
evidence: This is a direct statement about clinical outcomes in the study cohort.

claim: Patients had cardiac CMR examinations using a 1.5 T scanner (MAGNETOM Avanto; Siemens Healthcare, Erlangen, Germany) prior to ICD implantation.
source: Patients whose imaging data were retrospectively used in this study had cardiac CMR examinations using a 1.5 T scanner (MAGNETOM Avanto; Siemens Healthcare, Erlangen, Germany) prior to ICD implantation.
evidence: This is a statement about the imaging protocol used in the study.

claim: Short-axis LGE-CMR images with 2-mm in-plane and 8-mm z-axis resolution were acquired.
source: Short-axis LGE-CMR images with 2-mm in-plane and 8-mm z-axis resolution were acquired as previously described (Chu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the imaging protocol, supported by a citation to Chu et al., 2017.

claim: A single mid-ventricular short-axis postcontrast T1 map with 1.5-mm in-plane and 8-mm z-axis resolution was acquired during the same scan 12 min after gadolinium injection using a MOLLI sequence.
source: In addition, a single mid-ventricular short-axis postcontrast T1 map with 1.5-mm in-plane and 8-mm z-axis resolution was acquired during the same scan 12 min after gadolinium injection using a MOLLI sequence (Chu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the imaging protocol, supported by a citation to Chu et al., 2017.

claim: The LV myocardium was segmented from short-axis LGE-CMR in the CardioViz3D software using a validated semiautomatic landmark-based method.
source: The LV myocardium was segmented from short-axis LGE-CMR in the CardioViz3D software using a validated semiautomatic landmark-based method to define the boundaries of the endocardium and epicardium as described in previous virtual-heart projects by our team (Arevalo et al., 2016; Shade et al., 2020b; Cartoski et al., 2019)
evidence: This is a statement about the image processing methodology, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The RV was not reconstructed due to blood pool artifacts and the lack of hypertrophy and fibrotic substrate in HCM patients.
source: The RV was not reconstructed due to blood pool artifacts and the lack of hypertrophy and fibrotic substrate in HCM patients.
evidence: This is a statement about a methodological decision in model reconstruction.

claim: Regions in the T1 map with relaxation times <350 ms and 350–450 ms represent dense fibrosis (scar) and diffuse fibrosis, respectively.
source: Based on evidence in histopathological studies (Ellims et al., 2012; Iles et al., 2008; Mewton et al., 2011; Ellims et al., 2014), these regions in the T1 map represent dense fibrosis (scar) and diffuse fibrosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to histopathological studies (Ellims et al., 2012; Iles et al., 2008; Mewton et al., 2011; Ellims et al., 2014).

claim: High-resolution finite-element tetrahedral meshes, with an average resolution of 355 ± 69 μm, were constructed directly from the ventricular segmented images.
source: High-resolution finite-element tetrahedral meshes, with an average resolution of 355 ± 69 μm, were constructed directly from the ventricular segmented images using finite-element analysis software (Mimics Innovation Suite; Materialise, Leuven, Belgium)
evidence: This is a statement about the computational mesh generation process.

claim: The mesh resolution requirement in electrophysiological simulations is 300–400 μm to ensure stability of the solution.
source: The mesh resolution requirement in electrophysiological simulations is 300–400 μm to ensure stability of the solution, as demonstrated by a number of studies (Prassl et al., 2009; Plank et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Prassl et al., 2009 and Plank et al., 2008.

claim: Fiber orientations were applied to each computational mesh on a per-element basis using a rule-based approach validated using human fiber orientations acquired in histological and diffusion-tensor MRI studies.
source: Fiber orientations, unique to each patient-specific geometry, were applied to each computational mesh on a per-element basis using a rule-based approach (Bayer et al., 2012) validated using human fiber orientations acquired in histological and diffusion-tensor MRI studies.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bayer et al., 2012.

claim: In regions of nonfibrotic myocardium, the human ventricular myocyte model by ten Tusscher and Panfilov, 2006 was used, with added representation of INaL.
source: At the cellular level, in regions of nonfibrotic myocardium, the human ventricular myocyte model by ten Tusscher and Panfilov, 2006 was used, with added representation of INaL (O'Hara et al., 2011), as done in our previous studies (Cartoski et al., 2019; Shade et al., 2020a, Arevalo et al., 2016; Prakosa et al., 2018; Shade et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to ten Tusscher and Panfilov, 2006; O'Hara et al., 2011; and previous studies by the authors.

claim: For regions of diffuse fibrosis, ionic channel kinetics were modified based on data reported by Coppini et al., 2013.
source: For regions of diffuse fibrosis, we modified the ionic channel kinetics of the ten Tusscher model based on data reported by Coppini et al., 2013.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Coppini et al., 2013.

claim: Prolonged action potential duration and notch elevation following depolarization were observed in experimental recordings from myocytes in hyperthrophied regions acquired via myectomy.
source: In the latter study, prolonged action potential duration and notch elevation following depolarization were observed in experimental recordings from myocytes in hyperthrophied regions acquired via myectomy.
evidence: This claim refers to findings from Coppini et al., 2013.

claim: Regions of hypertrophy in the HCM heart are characterized with diffuse fibrotic remodeling, as per histopathological evidence.
source: As regions of hypertrophy in the HCM heart are also characterized with diffuse fibrotic remodeling, as per histopathological evidence (Galati et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Galati et al., 2016.

claim: Dense fibrosis was considered electrically inexcitable.
source: Dense fibrosis was considered electrically inexcitable.
evidence: This is a statement about a modeling assumption.

claim: Each virtual heart was paced sequentially from seven uniformly distributed endocardial LV locations using a validated rapid pacing protocol.
source: Each virtual heart was paced sequentially from seven uniformly distributed endocardial LV locations using a validated rapid pacing protocol described in detail in previous studies (Prakosa et al., 2018; Arevalo et al., 2016; Cartoski et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the simulation protocol, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: If VA was induced from at least one pacing site in a given personalized HCM virtual heart, the patient was considered at risk of VA.
source: If VA was induced from at least one pacing site in a given personalized HCM virtual heart, the patient was then considered at risk of VA.
evidence: This is a statement about the risk classification criterion used in the study.

claim: Simulation results were blind to clinical outcome.
source: Simulation results were blind to clinical outcome.
evidence: This is a statement about the study design to prevent bias.

claim: No statistically significant difference in regional hypertrophy was found at the septum (p = 0.61), anterior wall (p = 0.84), posterior wall (p = 0.94), and apex (p = 0.73) between heart models of patients with and without clinical VA.
source: No statistically significant difference in regional hypertrophy was found at the septum (p = 0.61), anterior wall (p = 0.84), posterior wall (p = 0.94), and apex (p = 0.73) between heart models of patients with and without clinical VA, as shown in Table 2.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the study's analysis, with reference to Table 2.

claim: The level of hypertrophy does not discriminate between arrhythmogenic and nonarrhythmogenic substrates in HCM patients.
source: These results indicated that the level of hypertrophy does not discriminate between arrhythmogenic and nonarrhythmogenic substrates in HCM patients.
evidence: This is an inference from the lack of significant differences in regional hypertrophy between groups.

claim: In three LGE-T1 virtual hearts from patients with known clinical VAs, a single VA morphology was induced in all three cases.
source: Figure 3 presents reentrant arrhythmias induced (from sites marked with stars) in three LGE-T1 virtual hearts from patients with known clinical VAs. In all three cases, a single VA morphology was induced.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulation results, with reference to Figure 3.
